diagnosis.summary: Request rates across product-service, cart-service, and order-service have all risen approximately 3x above their baselines over the past 4 minutes. Latency on both product-service and order-service has moved only marginally, and no 5xx errors have been recorded. The stack appears to be absorbing the increased load without degradation.
diagnosis.root_cause: A broad traffic spike affecting all three services simultaneously is the most likely root cause.
evidence: product-service request_rate rose from 15.0 rps to 45.1 rps, a 3x increase.
cart-service request_rate rose from 2.0 rps to 6.0 rps, also a 3x increase.
order-service request_rate rose from 2.9 rps to 8.8 rps, approximately a 3x increase.
product-service p95 latency moved from 24 ms to 31 ms, a 29% increase, remaining well within normal range.
product-service error_rate_5xx is 0.0 at both baseline and current, with no errors observed.
order-service p95 latency moved from 58 ms to 61 ms, a 5% increase, with no meaningful degradation.
recommended_actions: Monitor lambda_throttle_count on all three services; the shared account concurrency limit could become a constraint if request rates continue to rise.
Watch product-service db_consumed_read_capacity and read_throttle_events, as GET /products scans the Products table and reads grow with traffic.
If latency and error rates remain near baseline, continue monitoring without making changes, as the stack is currently absorbing the load.
If throttling appears or latency climbs, set rate and burst limits on the API Gateway stage to protect the stack while the source of the traffic is identified.
If product-service reads approach the provisioned capacity of the Products table, raise its provisioned read capacity or switch it to on-demand mode.
